newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria premier seeks Paris club debt rollover.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria premier seeks Paris club debt rollover.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski said on Thursday he had sent a letter to the Paris Club of official creditors seeking to rollover up to $50 million of this year's dues.
"I sent a letter asking the official creditors of the Paris Club...to rollover the payments for next year," Sofianski told reporters after a cabinet session.
He said Bulgaria sought to reschedule up to $50 million due from part of the non-rescheduled payments.
Bulgaria has so far, paid these amounts regularly, but an economic crisis from continuous mishandling of the economy has depleted its reserves.
Under three agreements to reschedule a $1.2- billion debt owed to the Paris club by 1995, Bulgaria is due to pay official creditors $126 million this year.
"We expect our creditors to receive this in goodwill as a rescheduling request was something the international financial community anticipated," Sofianski said.
On Wednesday, Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said Bulgaria would seek a possible rescheduling of other Paris Club payments as well.

Bulgaria is likely to reach a preliminary funding agreement with an International Monetary Fund mission currently in Sofia that will help the interim cabinet overcome a grave financial crisis. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
